notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0011] Apply approval threshold to support-initiated refunds: Refunds above 500.00 require a second approver; raise BillingError("approval_required") when approved_by is missing.
  Accept keyword-only approved_by=None, compare the rounded amount against a 500.00 threshold, and raise BillingError("approval_required", str(amount)) only when the amount exceeds it and no approver is supplied. Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval.
- [rb-0001] Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected because the team requires ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent).
  Before returning any monetary Decimal, check the repo's money module for a rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and wrap the final value with it. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
- [rb-0004] Match existing error codes and validation style before writing new code: Grep the codebase for BillingError usages and isinstance checks to mirror established conventions rather than inventing new ones.
  Before implementing validation, search sibling modules for existing error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and type-check patterns. Reusing the same codes and message formats keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on error codes.
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency key before any state validation: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating payment state or amounts.
  Scan audit.events(<event_name>) for a matching idempotency_key at the very top of the function; if found, return the original record unchanged. Only after that do state/amount checks, and always include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.
- [rb-0012] Serialize Decimal amounts as float in audit entries: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal, so audit fields carrying money must be cast with float(amount).
  When calling audit.record for refunds or credits, pass amount=float(amount) and refunded_amount=float(payment.refunded_amount). Keep Decimal arithmetic internally via to_money/round_money; only convert at the audit boundary.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module and existing helpers before implementing: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py revealed ZERO, to_money, and round_money, which the accepted solution reused instead of raw arithmetic.
  When a task involves amounts, open the money/utility module first and reuse its constants and converters (ZERO, to_money, round_money) so behavior matches the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for rounding and conversion
item.description: When implementing monetary functions, use the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers instead of raw float arithmetic.
item.content: Search the codebase for money utilities (e.g. to_money, round_money, ZERO) and import them rather than reimplementing rounding. Convert inputs to Decimal via to_money before computing, and round the final result with round_money to avoid float drift.

item.title: Match existing error conventions for validation
item.description: Raise the project's domain error class with a short machine-readable code, following sibling modules.
item.content: Grep for the error class (e.g. BillingError) and how it's raised elsewhere; use the same pattern `raise BillingError("code", str(value))` with a snake_case code. Validate bounds before computing so invalid inputs fail fast.

item.title: Explore tests and sibling modules before implementing
item.description: Reading existing tests, errors, and related modules reveals expected types, error codes, and conventions.
item.content: Before writing a new function, inspect the target file, its tests, the errors module, and modules with similar logic. This surfaces helper functions, expected return types (Decimal vs float), and validation style, reducing rework.
